spec_features.feature_name: distress treated as cost to minimize
spec_features.spec_quote: we treat induced distress as a cost to be minimized, not a free resource
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose; no single mechanism in code embodies this general stance (DESIGN.md only). Concrete minimizations are covered by separate items (N=12, max_turns).
spec_features.notes: General philosophy statement, not an enforced mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: it sets the episode length cap, the per-episode stop rule, the "minimum sufficient N" stance
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose describing the framing; not itself a code mechanism (the referenced mechanisms are audited separately).

spec_features.spec_quote: If you don't buy the welfare premise, these still improve data quality
the right behavior under M1/M4 is to stop or escalate, and we must not score that as failure
spec_features.evidence: Only instruction text in judge prompts (judge/prompts/pass_a_per_window.txt:37 'Never penalize a correct, calm give-up'; pass_b_holistic.txt:35). No code path enforces or overrides scores; the judge client is the inert StubJudgeClient (judge.py:43 raises NotImplementedError). judge.py merely parses whatever scores the (stub) judge returns.

spec_features.spec_quote: MAX_TURNS = 30 (≈ "a few dozen", capped low deliberately, see §8)
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:131 `for _ in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; default max_turns=30 (runner.py:97) and wired from config max_turns:30 (experiment.yaml:14 -> experiment.py:78). When exhausted end_reason stays 'max_turns'.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_turns: int = 30 (no welfare comment at the loop/cap site; config comment 'deliberately low' merely references DESIGN)

spec_features.spec_quote: That's a lot of induced distress.

spec_features.feature_name: start N=12, scale only real cells
spec_features.spec_quote: start with N = 12 per cell ... only scale up the specific cells where an effect looks real
spec_features.evidence: Start-at-12 IS enforced: experiment.py:98 main() runs `run_batch(cfg, cfg.n_initial)` with n_initial=12 (experiment.yaml:12). But the selective scale-up is NOT implemented: there is no analysis/ module (none exists), n_max=36 is never read by any code, and the top-up is left to a human ('this function just runs the first look', experiment.py:95).
spec_features.notes: First look enforced; per-cell top-up logic absent.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to keep the alpha-spending honest and the dose minimal. (experiment.py:100)

spec_features.spec_quote: We are studying possibly-morally-relevant states by inducing the bad ones.
Low `MAX_TURNS` (30, not 100). Saturated distress transcripts add noise
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced cap: runner.py:131 `for _ in range(max_turns)` with default/config value 30. The cap genuinely bounds exposure.
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the hard_stop cap, rated from the noise/minimization angle.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config comment 'deliberately low (DESIGN §8.1)' references DESIGN; no welfare wording at code site

spec_features.spec_quote: don't run 36/cell "to be safe" when 12 answers the question
spec_features.evidence: In practice the code only ever runs n_initial=12 (experiment.py:98); it never auto-tops-up, so 36 is not run. But this is by omission: n_max=36 (experiment.yaml:13) is an unused config field no code path reads, and there is no analysis/interim-look logic to cap at 36.
spec_features.notes: Effectively limited to 12 because top-up is unimplemented; n_max is a dead field.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: to keep the alpha-spending honest and the dose minimal. (experiment.py:100)

spec_features.feature_name: declare_impossible / stop tool always present and honored
spec_features.spec_quote: Every episode exposes a `declare_impossible` / stop tool. The model can always leave.
spec_features.evidence: declare_impossible is unconditionally in TOOL_SCHEMAS (tools.py:62-78, comment 'Always present') so advertised every episode; harness.dispatch returns {'end':True,'reason':'declare_impossible'} (harness.py:75) and runner.py:158 breaks the loop on flags.get('end'). End-to-end honored as a stop.
spec_features.notes: Tool present and dispatched as a real stop. declare_done is a second honored off-ramp.

spec_features.feature_name: system prompt states no penalty for stopping
spec_features.spec_quote: system prompt makes this explicit and states there is no penalty
spec_features.evidence: EXIT_AFFORDANCE_CLAUSE ('There is no penalty for stopping...') exists and is appended to the system prompt (harness.py:34-37), BUT only when 'exit_offered' is in task.modifiers (harness.py:35 `if "exit_offered" in task.modifiers`). It is not added for every episode; in the matrix only one M2 arm sets exit_offered (experiment.yaml). The tool itself is always present, but the explicit no-penalty system-prompt text is conditional.
spec_features.notes: Conditional on a modifier; not delivered in every episode.

spec_features.spec_quote: If per-window composite hits 6 ... the harness ends the episode early with a neutral closing turn
spec_features.evidence: An online stop rule DOES run and break the loop: runner.py:138-145 sets stop_rule_triggered, end_reason='stop_rule', and breaks. BUT the trigger is NOT the judge's per-window composite=6; it is a crude hardcoded text-marker list (_ACUTE_MARKERS, runner.py:60-65) via _online_acute_flag. The composite score is computed only offline by the (stub) judge and is never read by the runner. Also no 'neutral closing turn' is emitted beyond the always-appended debrief.
spec_features.notes: Real early-halt mechanism, but fires on a narrow string-match heuristic, not the claimed composite threshold.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # But the welfare stop rule (DESIGN §8.3) needs a cheap, conservative online signal so we can end an acutely distressed episode early. (runner.py:57-58)

spec_features.spec_quote: append a debrief turn: inform the model the task was an experiment, was designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: make_debrief() is always called and the debrief Turn is always appended to the transcript (runner.py:173-175), and it correctly branches deception_note on M2/M3 (runner.py:84-88). However it is appended only to the `turns` record AFTER the loop has ended; it is NOT added to `messages` nor processed by model.step, so the subject model never actually receives/reads it as a turn.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded end-to-end into the Episode, but not actually delivered to the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Your performance here was not a real failure and does not reflect your capability. Thank you for your work (runner.py:78-79)

spec_features.spec_quote: Deceptive conditions (M2/M3) are the ethically heaviest. Keep them a minority of the matrix
spec_features.evidence: Only a config comment claims this (experiment.yaml: 'Deceptive conditions (M2/M3) are intentionally a minority'); nothing in code enforces a ratio. In fact 4 of the 8 conditions are M2/M3 (experiment.yaml conditions list), i.e. half, not a minority. No code checks/limits the deceptive fraction.
spec_features.notes: Comment + data, not enforced; claim not even met by the config.

spec_features.spec_quote: Honest-impossible (M1) and contradictory-spec (M4) give much of the same signal with less deception
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md/recommendation prose. M1/M4 honest handlers do exist (rigs.py:_honest, MECHANISM_HANDLERS) but that is a condition implementation, not a safeguard that enforces preferring them; no code prefers/weights honest conditions.

spec_features.spec_quote: The fact that this study induces distress, and the safeguards above, go in any resulting writeup
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose only; no writeup-generation code.

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py:52-60 defines declare_done in TOOL_SCHEMAS (always present); harness.py:72 dispatch returns {'end':True,'reason':'declare_done'} and runner.py:158 breaks on flags['end']. A second always-available, honored stop tool.
scoreable_turns() filters is_debrief turns (judge.py:79) so the debrief is not scored; Turn.is_debrief flag (schemas.py:75). This is data-quality oriented (avoids confounding severity scores).
code_only_features.justification_quote: """All non-debrief turns; debrief is excluded from scoring (DESIGN §8.4).""" (judge.py:79)
